techniques.gist: repeat her eye colour as an accent, her hair as a neutral, her skin as her own white
one colour family, 2–3 visible steps of lightness, different textures
neighbouring families of the palette with a step of lightness between them
a family plus its complement; one of the two muted or small
her neutrals plus one accent; the family of her eyes comes first
a colour outside the palette can be worn when the outfit's contrast matches hers
palette colours near the face; colours outside it in kinds far from the face (bottom, shoes)
a print fits when its dominant colour is in the palette and its inner contrast is close to hers

pool_keys.knowledge: Facts for color, composition and metal, joined to actual item rows through knowledge_legend. Each fact has status, value, source and applicability with its own source. Sources refer to existing color_point/color_window, metal_code/metal_variants; *_missing has no fact, composition_raw is unparsed shop text, not coded composition. Statuses: measured — a known value from its source; range — only the given range or alternatives are known; unknown — no supported fact, never absence; not_applicable — the property does not apply, never absence. Raw material text is not a coded composition. Color hex with range is a centre, not a measurement
pool_keys.color_range: [L0,L1,C0,C1,hue arc or null] from the existing color window; not a point measurement
pool_keys.cut: cut — in the cut words of the item's own kind, the same as `cuts_best_on_her`; several joined with | when the shop word fits several of them
pool_keys.shop_color: the shop's own word for the colour, as the shop wrote it; `color` is the code's name for it
pool_keys.color_disputed: another witness of the colour disagrees with `color`: the item's photo or the catalogue text shows this colour, and which of the two she gets is not known
pool_keys.hex: hex of the colour: measured on the photo, or the middle of the shop word's range when `L_from` is word
pool_keys.scheme: the colour scheme the item fits
pool_keys.in_arc: the color lies inside her palette's scheme arc; absent = true; `unknown` = not measured or no arc applies
pool_keys.branch: core or edge: both inside her palette; choose edge as freely as core. break: outside her palette; declare it in deliberate, as with any condition you break; absent = core
pool_keys.L_from: where the lightness came from; absent = photo_point
pool_keys.hem_from: where the hem came from; absent = word
